There are multiple things that a seller MUST disclose when selling a house in Ontario.  Material Latent Defects (Safety & Habitability Issues):
 Structural damage (e.g., severe foundation cracks behind drywall, compromised load-bearing walls).
 Hidden electrical hazards (e.g., active knob-and-tube or aluminum wiring behind walls).
 Serious plumbing or septic system failures.
 Environmental or health hazards (e.g., toxic mold, asbestos, lead paint, active termite infestations).
 Underground storage tanks (e.g., a buried oil tank on the property).
 History of major water damage or seasonal basement flooding.
 Any history of the property being used as an illegal drug lab (e.g., a former grow-op).
 Government & Municipal Actions:
 Outstanding municipal work orders or building code violations.
 Illegal renovations done without proper building permits (such as an unpermitted basement apartment).
 Notice of upcoming local zoning changes or expropriations affecting the land.
 Answers to Direct Questions:
 Honest, truthful answers to any direct questions asked by a prospective buyer or their agent (lying or omitting facts when asked directly is considered fraudulent misrepresentation).
 Information Shared with Your Realtor:
 Any material latent defects you disclose to your own real estate agent (by law under TRESA, agents must disclose these to potential buyers).

Yesterday we said goodbye to Nunu 🤍
I picked Nu (formerly known as Newnew) up from the Toronto Humane Society on April 21, 2018. I remember seeing an email come in about a dog who had been in the shelter since September and was brought back by her last foster family. I selfishly wanted a new foster dog because I was going through a very difficult time in my life and I wanted emotional support. If you ask anyone that knew the bond Nu and I shared, they’d tell you that we saved each other. When I met Nu she had a laundry list of medical and behavioural issues - within a year the team at THS asked me if I’d adopt her because she had morphed into a completely different dog. 
Nu was the most special girl. She was also looking out for me (and looking for me). When I was testifying in court, Nu was right there by my side. She wasn’t thrilled when I brought @braandonly and his chaotic energy into her life, but they too quickly formed their own special bond - and she was definitely not thrilled when we brought home her even more chaotic little brother, Theo. But she was the best big sister and loved him so much. 
The biggest downfall of my relationship with Nu was that I realized very quickly on that losing her would destroy me. She was my soul dog. Saying goodbye to Nu was the hardest thing I’ve ever done and I will spend every day missing her. 
Rest easy my sweet girl, I hope you’ve found the freshest grass to roll around in and so many sticks to destroy. I hope all your pain is gone and you can run around chasing and trying to eat small dogs and cats. I will always love you.

caption:
This is Nunu. And we had a contract - an agreement of sorts. 

Our contract was simple “I will follow, I will trust you, to get me through the small moments to make it to my favourite ones.”

You weren’t always excited for me. You saved all that love for mom. But that was okay. 

I was the bridge. 

In the beginning I was just a strange boy who would bother you. You would look to your mom “who is this guy you keep bringing around?”

But as the days, months and years passed our relationship grew and our contract was solidified. 

I earned your trust to lead you through the transitionary periods throughout the day.

Especially as times got harder. 

You trusted me to get you up the stairs as they became steeper. 

To move and adapt as your strides became smaller. Your legs a little weaker. 

To keep you honest when you tried to be lazy. 

But to pause in the moments when you said “I’m a little sore.” 

To keep you included as Theo entered our lives. 

To make you work a little to get your dinner. 

To guide you through the walk so you could bolt past me and get to mom. 

These were moments you, Nu, trusted me with. 

On your last day you trusted me one last time. One last honoured contract. 

One more “Okay, dad.” 

You trusted me one more time.
Slow, quiet, and around the block. 
Even when your body was tired.
Even when you didn’t stop to sniff.
You followed, and I led, just like we always did.

But I didn’t know that this time was for me. 

It wasn’t just “Okay, dad.” 

It was “Okay dad, for you.”

You trusted me with your safety. 

With guidance. 

And you gave it back to me as a gift you couldn’t tell me.

That meant everything to me.

Rest easy Nu. We all love you so much. ❤️🕊️
